name: WENO5-JS, finite-difference flux form
source: Jiang and Shu, J. Comput. Phys. 126 (1996), eqs. (2.10), (2.15)-(2.16), (3.2)-(3.4); critical points: Henrick, Aslam and Powers, J. Comput. Phys. 207 (2005)

claims.why: eps fixed, beta = O(dx^2): omega_k - d_k = O(dx^2), candidate errors O(dx^3), so O(dx^5)
the linear (d_k) part alone has a non-zero dx^5 term
both stencils in the generic regime, weight expansions uniform in the stencil centre, so the dx^4 terms cancel in the difference
f' != 0: every beta_k = (f' dx)^2 (1 + O(dx^2)), so omega_k = d_k + O(dx^2) (Jiang-Shu (3.8))
Henrick et al.: omega_k = d_k + O(dx) at f' = 0, rate 3
Henrick et al.: rate 3, not 4; the i-1/2 stencil (f'(x_{i-1}) = -f'' dx) has O(dx) weight errors that are not those of the i+1/2 stencil
convex weights of third-order candidates, each error O(dx^3) after the difference, leading beta terms positive
eps comparable to beta = O(dx^4): leading weights still d_k, O(dx) errors as with eps = 0
as eps = 0 with the O(dx) weight errors scaled by beta/(eps + beta); they do not vanish
eps = dx^2 >> beta = O(dx^4): alpha_k = d_k eps^-2 (1 - 2 beta_k/eps + ...); the dx^2 part of beta_k/eps is the same for every k at both stencils, so omega_k - d_k = O(dx^3)
beta_k = (f' dx)^2 + O(dx^4) for every k, eps + beta_k = (c + f'^2) dx^2 (1 + O(dx^2)), omega_k = d_k + O(dx^2), uniform in the centre
eps fixed and beta = O(dx^4): omega_k - d_k = O(dx^4), error O(dx^4 dx^3 / dx); the order drop needs eps small against beta

critical point at the stencil centre: beta_k = (13/12) f''^2 dx^4 (1 + 2(k-1)(f'''/f'') dx + O(dx^2)), so omega_k - d_k = d_k (f'''/f'') dx (4/5 - 4(k-1)) + O(dx^2); with the candidate errors A_k dx^3, A = (1/4, -1/12, 1/12) f''', sum_k (omega_k - d_k) A_k = 0 at order dx^4, so the point error is O(dx^5); the drop to 3 is a property of the difference, not of one reconstruction
the dx^5 term of the linear part does not vanish at f' = 0
convex combination of third-order candidates; leading betas (121/108, 1/36, 121/108) f'''^2 dx^6 positive
f' = f'' = 0: leading betas (121/108, 1/36, 121/108) f'''^2 dx^6 differ, so the leading weights are not d_k and sum_k omega_k A_k != 0 at dx^3
leading-order sketch only: the two stencils have different O(1) weight limits, so O(dx^3)/dx; not derived further
same sketch: the dx^3 terms of the two reconstructions have different coefficients
